material_changes.hypothesis_change: Promote Gaussian splats from research-only capture representation to a standardized optional visual-delivery layer, while retaining explicit mesh proxies for collision, physics, selection, navigation and WebGL fallback.

evidence.claim: KHR_gaussian_splatting is marked Complete and Ratified in the maintained specification repository.
Three.js ships GLTFGaussianSplatLoaderExtension for KHR_gaussian_splatting; the GaussianSplat runtime path requires WebGPURenderer.
Blender 5.3 imports and renders 3D Gaussian splats using a native point-cloud splat type from PLY/SPZ, but currently has no splat export and documents transform/rendering limitations.

material_changes.contradiction: Official Khronos specification text says Complete/Ratified while recent Khronos event material still calls Gaussian Splatting a Release Candidate. Blender can ingest/render splats but not export them, and Three.js native KHR splat rendering currently requires WebGPU.
material_changes.engineering_implication: Use KHR_gaussian_splatting GLB as the preferred standards-track research interchange where supported, retain SPZ as a compact capture/import format, and always pair captured splats with a semantic mesh/proxy layer. Feature-detect WebGPU and never make splats the sole production representation yet.
material_changes.experiment_definition: Take one captured room/architectural subject and test the same reconstruction as KHR_gaussian_splatting GLB, SPZ and semantic mesh proxy across Blender 5.3 and Three.js WebGPU; measure appearance/SH fidelity, transforms, bytes, load time, GPU memory, mobile/WebGL fallback and interaction/collision behavior.
material_changes.priority_change: Insert ahead of EXP-GLTF21-COMPOSE-001 because the interchange path is now concrete enough to validate cheaply and directly.

material_changes.hypothesis_change: Procedural node systems should increasingly have diffable, reviewable source authority rather than opaque .blend files being the only source of truth.

evidence.source: Blender Developers Blog, Geometry Nodes Workshop September 2026
evidence.claim: The Blender team documents external libraries such as Molecular Nodes storing node groups as Python code via nodebpy, discusses Git diff/merge workflows, plans asset splitting into one .blend per asset, and is exploring export nodes, lists, graph processing and reusable node-group compatibility.
Current Geometry Nodes work includes bake path templating and ongoing asset/workflow changes, reinforcing a more automatable procedural content pipeline.

material_changes.contradiction: The strongest workflow ideas are partly workshop direction/WIP rather than stable Blender contracts. nodebpy proves the pattern in an external library, not universal round-trip fidelity for every Blender node system.
material_changes.engineering_implication: Prototype text-source procedural assets plus generated .blend artifacts and one-asset-per-file packaging. Do not migrate production authority until round-trip fidelity, deterministic builds, code review usefulness and CI behavior are demonstrated.
material_changes.experiment_definition: Choose one Gaudí parametric element and one KONA procedural asset; represent node graph/source in diffable text, generate the Blender asset, rebuild twice for determinism, compare geometry/material hashes, and evaluate Git review/merge ergonomics.
material_changes.priority_change: Fold the narrower EXP-BLENDER52-BUNDLES-001 into this broader source-authority experiment.
